proposal.description: Latched-trip solid indication waits until the supervisor has left the switching states, as if a latch only counted once the converter had stopped, so the CPLD's own trip in S_SS/S_RUN is not shown solid at once
proposal.reason: When latch_assert (or latch_state) rises while ss_active or run_active is still high, Red_LED1 shows the strike blink or stays dark instead of going solid on the next clock. It goes solid only after the supervisor leaves S_SS/S_RUN.

proposal.description: Running indication takes 'running' from the power-good comparator instead of run_active, mixing up 'output in regulation' with 'converter switching'
proposal.reason: Green_LED stays lit in S_OFF or S_HICCUP for as long as pgood is still high (for example while the rail decays after a hiccup entry), and goes dark in S_RUN whenever pgood drops, though the converter is running with no fault.

why: make lint already catches it: make lint: UNUSEDSIGNAL

proposal.description: Undervoltage indicator is shown only while the converter is not switching, as if input UVLO only mattered once it was holding the converter off
proposal.reason: If uvlo_state rises while the supervisor is in S_SS or S_RUN, Red_LED3 stays dark until the supervisor leaves those states, though the header says it follows the input undervoltage condition.

proposal.description: Live-fault mask on Green is applied only during soft-start, because the designer stretched the window-trip argument ('a fault takes the supervisor out of S_RUN on the next edge') to cover every fault in S_RUN
proposal.reason: When OTP, UVLO, latch_state or latch_assert goes live while run_active is high, Green_LED stays lit until the supervisor leaves S_RUN, instead of going dark on the next clock.

proposal.description: Over-temperature is treated as a terminal latched trip and lights Red_LED1 solid, as if a thermal shutdown always fired the SCR
proposal.reason: While otp_state is live and no latch is set, Red_LED1 is lit solid instead of dark, or instead of blinking when strikes are outstanding. This hides the strike pattern and shows a non-latched OTP as a board that has given up.
